newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares rise as profit-taking wanes.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares rise as profit-taking wanes.

text.p: Egyptian share prices recouped some recent losses on Thursday as investors reconsidered a selling spree and waited for dividends instead, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index rose 0.89 points to 234.79 on high turnover of 107.92 million pounds ($31.74 million).
Shares worth 9.4 million pounds of privatised East Delta Flour Mills were also listed on Thursday.

"No one wants to sell anything and the market is dry. They feel prices are not quite right and many people are holding onto their shares until November when some companies will give out dividends," said broker Sherif Cararah of Hermes EFG.
New listing Central and West Flour Mills was the day's most active share, rising 0.26 pounds to 47.30 despite what brokers said was mainly speculative trade.

Speculators, who sell their shares for a quick profit shortly after buying them during the state's IPOs, also hit recently privatised Memphis Pharmaceuticals and Chemical Industries, which lost 3.00 pounds to end at 61.03.
Rumoured foreign interest in National Societe Generale Bank helped push shares 4.75 pounds up to 460.00.
"The bank's shares have a P/E ratio of eight which is lower than the market's nine or 10. There's also some liquidity in the share which is why we're seeing activity," Cararah said.
Brokers said international investors also had their eye on Egypt's only cigarette maker Eastern Tobacco but the stock ended unchanged at 47.00 on trading worth 4.06 million.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell off a record 369.17 points to 368.65 on Thursday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 160.92 to 159.80 points.
